{{Short description|Discontinued audience response system}}
'''Microsoft Pulse''' (previously branded as '''Bing Pulse''') is an [[audience response system]] from [[Microsoft]]. On June 30, 2017, the service was discontinued as a free public service. It is now only available as part of [[Skype for Business]] Skype Meeting Broadcast.

Note: the domain https://pulse.microsoft.com is unrelated to the Pulse service and provides news and information for Microsoft Benelux customers.

Bing Pulse is an audience engagement technology for live feedback from audiences of any size, during any event, on any web-enabled device, and on any [[Web browser|browser]].<ref>https://www.linkedin.com/company/8570744?trk=tyah&trkInfo=tarId%3A1418329239281%2Ctas%3Abing%20puls%2Cidx%3A2-1-4 {{Self-published source|date=June 2022}}</ref> Bing Pulse gives viewers the ability to respond every five seconds, and as often as they want, to the content they're hearing and seeing. Pulse also gives users the opportunity to have their say in polls and see how others are responding in real time.<ref name=Bing-Pulse-Features-Smallbiztrends>{{cite news|last=Sophy|first=Joshua|title=Bing Pulse Lets You Measure the Mood.|url=http://smallbiztrends.com/2014/12/bing-pulse-measure-mood.html|newspaper=Small Businesses Trends|date=9 December 2014}}</ref><ref>https://www.linkedin.com/company/8570744?trk=tyah&trkInfo=tarId%3A1418329239281%2Ctas%3Abing%20puls%2Cidx%3A2-1-4 {{Self-published source|date=June 2022}}</ref> 
Bing Pulse was unveiled on February 12, 2013, during Fox's broadcast of the [[2013 State of the Union]]. Since its inception, Bing Pulse has generated more than 35 million votes from participants across the US.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.bing.com/search/2014/12/03/bing-pulse-2-0-gives-consumers-a-voice-delivers-real-time-audience-insights-to-broadcasters-and-live-event-organizers/|title = Bing Pulse 2.0 gives consumers a voice, delivers real-time audience insights to broadcasters and live event organizers | date=3 December 2014 }}</ref> Bing Pulse 2.0 was released in beta on December 3, 2014.<ref name=PC-Magazine-Bing-Pulse-2.0>{{cite news|last=Moscaritolo|first=Angela|title=Microsoft Opens Bing Pulse 2.0 Real-Time Polling Platform. Let audience members share opinions in real-time during a live event and push out poll questions at any time. |url=https://www.pcmag.com/article2/0,2817,2473076,00.asp|newspaper=PC Magazine|date=3 December 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.bing.com/search/2014/12/03/bing-pulse-2-0-gives-consumers-a-voice-delivers-real-time-audience-insights-to-broadcasters-and-live-event-organizers/|title = Bing Pulse 2.0 gives consumers a voice, delivers real-time audience insights to broadcasters and live event organizers | date=3 December 2014 }}</ref> Notable changes included a self-service option for users to purchase and use Bing Pulse through the product's website, and several product improvements, including sharper consumer graphics and experience; a responsive, multi-device design; and more flexibility in visualizations.

In December 2015 Microsoft announced that they would drop the [[Bing (search engine)|Bing]] branding in favour of the general "Microsoft" brand and would integrate other Microsoft services such as [[Microsoft OneNote|OneNote]], [[Skype]], [[Skype for Business]] and [[Microsoft Azure|Azure]]. Alongside the rebranding Microsoft announced that the service would be focused beyond merely real-time voting.<ref name=Beta-News-Bing-Pulse-Rebranded-As-Microsoft-Pulse>{{cite news|last=Fagioli|first=Brian|title=Bing Pulse rebrands as Microsoft Pulse.|url=http://betanews.com/2015/12/15/bing-microsoft-pulse/|newspaper=Beta News|date=15 December 2015}}</ref>

== Features==
[[File:Bing-pulse-website-image.jpg|thumb|Bing Pulse is available on any device form factor during a meeting or event.]]
Bing Pulse has both pulsing and polling functions. Pulse is a content rating tool that allows viewers to express their opinion continuously at any moment during a live program or event.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pulse.bing.com/faq/|title = Ambassadors of the airwaves}}</ref> Poll questions provide real-time, customizable technology that allows for expanded questioning throughout an event to gain deeper insights and data. Bing Pulse allows unlimited participants and doesn't collect end-users’ personal data. 
Additional Bing Pulse features include:
* All-in-one real-time voting and polling, [[social media]] integration, and immediate visualized insights
* Smart analytics that segment audience data by gender, political affiliation, geography, or other criteria
* Integration into websites, live streams, broadcast channels and [[Bing.com]] with embeddable iFrame and [[API]] availability
* Negative results are accumulated and highlighted
* No charge to participants using the service
* Video Pulse, an analytics tool that can collect feedback from any recorded video<ref name=Microsoft-Pulse-Multi-Channel-Video-Pulse-March-2016>{{cite news|last=Media|first=NewBay|title=Microsoft Pulse Announces the Upcoming Availability of Video Pulse at SXSWedu 2016. This section of Multichannel. com, "The PR Feed", contains original press releases issued by various companies and industry organizations. The releases are not reviewed or edited by the editorial staff of Multichannel News.|url=http://www.multichannel.com/prfeed/microsoft-pulse-announces-upcoming-availability-video-pulse-sxswedu-2016/403127|newspaper=Multichannel|date=7 March 2016}}</ref>
* Educators can upload recorded class sessions and lectors and say whether or not the attending students can understand it or comprehend key ideas at the time
* Companies can test how potential customers respond to an upcoming advertisement campaign or other digital content through an uploaded video 
* Producers can gauge reactions to mobile videos regardless of when the video was viewed<ref name=Microsoft-Power-User-Microsoft-Pulse-Video-Pulse>{{cite news|last=Viswav|first=Pradeep|title=Microsoft Announces The Upcoming Availability Of Video Pulse Service.|url=http://mspoweruser.com/microsoft-announces-upcoming-availability-video-pulse/|newspaper=Microsoft PowerUser|date=8 March 2016}}</ref>

== Usage ==
Bing Pulse was first used in partnership with Fox's broadcast of the 2013 State of the Union.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.bing.com/search/2013/02/08/introducing-the-bing-pulse-and-the-bing-interactive-state-of-the-union-experience/|title = Introducing the Bing Pulse and the Bing Interactive State of the Union Experience | date=8 February 2013 }}</ref><ref name=Engadget-Bing-Pulse-Launch>{{cite news|last=Alvarez|first=Edgar|title=Bing Pulse launching with help from Fox News, aims to make State of the Union speech more interactive.|url=https://www.engadget.com/2013/02/09/bing-pulse-fox-news-state-of-the-union/|newspaper=Engadget|date=9 February 2013}}</ref><ref name=WinBeta-Bing-Pulse-CNN>{{cite news|last=Al-Riyami|first=Fahad|title=Microsoft launches Bing Pulse to power CNN's 2014 Elections coverage.|url=http://www.winbeta.org/news/microsoft-launches-bing-pulse-power-cnns-2014-elections-coverage|newspaper=WinBeta|date=21 October 2014}}</ref> Since then, Bing Pulse has been incorporated into content with several cable news networks, generating more than 35 million audience votes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.bing.com/search/2014/12/03/bing-pulse-2-0-gives-consumers-a-voice-delivers-real-time-audience-insights-to-broadcasters-and-live-event-organizers/|title = Bing Pulse 2.0 gives consumers a voice, delivers real-time audience insights to broadcasters and live event organizers | date=3 December 2014 }}</ref><ref name=TechCrunch-Bing-Pulse-35-Million-Participants>{{cite news|last=Ha|first=Anthony|title=Microsoft Makes Its Audience Polling Service Bing Pulse Available To Anyone.|url=https://techcrunch.com/2014/12/03/bing-pulse-2-0/|newspaper=TechCrunch (America On-Line)|date=3 December 2014}}</ref> 
Today, Bing Pulse is available on a self-serve basis. Anyone in the [[United States]], [[United Kingdom]], and [[India]] can set up a Pulse (additional countries will be added soon), and anyone worldwide can participate in a Pulse.

=== CNN ===
On October 21, 2014, Microsoft and [[CNN]] announced a partnership to include Bing Pulse as part of CNN's broadcast coverage of the [[United States elections, 2014|2014 US elections]] through to the 2016 Presidential elections.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.bing.com/search/?p=69083|title = Bing Search Blog &#124; This is a place devoted to giving you deeper insight into the news, trends, people and technology behind Bing | date=3 October 2025 }}</ref> During the 2014 election season, CNN used Bing Pulse in their broadcast of the Florida gubernatorial debate and the New Hampshire U.S. Senatorial Debate. Previously, Bing Pulse had been incorporated into CNN's broadcast of President Obama's National ISIS address<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pulse.bing.com/?post_type=casestudies&p=1711|title=Ambassadors of the airwaves}}</ref> and a televised conversation between [[Bill Clinton]] and [[Erin Burnett]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pulse.bing.com/bing-pulse-unearths-gender-differences-partisanship-at-the-2014-clinton-global-initiative/|title = Ambassadors of the airwaves}}</ref>

=== FOX ===
[[Fox News Channel|Fox]] built on their momentum from the 2013 State of the Union, opting to use Pulse during the 2014 [[State of the Union]] address as well. Additionally, Bing Pulse was a regular feature on Special Report with [[Bret Baier]] from July 2013 to January 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.microsoft.com/firehose/2013/09/16/use-bing-pulse-to-join-the-conversation-on-the-fox-news-channels-special-report-with-bret-baier/|title = Stories &#124; Microsoft news, features, events, and press materials}}</ref><ref name=Bing-Pulse-Fox-News-State-of-the-Union>{{cite news|last=Wilson|first=Mark|title=Bing Pulse to be used by Fox News to gauge reaction to the State of the Union address.|url=http://www.winbeta.org/news/bing-pulse-be-used-fox-news-gauge-reaction-state-union-address|newspaper=WinBeta|date=28 January 2014}}</ref>

=== NBC ===
Pulse was a featured part of [[MSNBC]]'s The Great Debate series, where the audience was able to vote in real-time during a debate about the NSA held at the 2014 [[Aspen Ideas Festival]].<ref name=Bing-Pulse-Aspen>{{cite news|title=Engaging the audience. Microsoft showcased Bing Pulse at this year's International Confex, we catch up with Greg Shaw, senior director of corporate strategy on the self-service audience engagement tool.  |url=http://www.exhibitionnews.co.uk/featuredetails/349/engaging-the-audience|newspaper=Exhibition News|date=14 May 2014}}</ref> Additionally, CNBC incorporated Bing Pulse into a televised panel session held during the 2014 [[Clinton Foundation|Clinton Global Initiative]] annual meeting.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pulse.bing.com/cnbcconsumers/|title=Ambassadors of the airwaves}}</ref><ref name=Geek-Wire-Bing-Pulse-Clinton-Annual-Meeting>{{cite news|last=Bishop|first=Todd|title=Clintons using Microsoft 'Bing Pulse' for real-time audience voting at annual meeting.|url=http://www.geekwire.com/2014/clintons-using-microsoft-bing-pulse-real-time-voting-annual-meeting/|newspaper=GeekWire|date=24 June 2014}}</ref><ref name=Search-Marketing-Daily-Bing-Pulse-Clinton-Foundation>{{cite news|last=Sullivan|first=Laurie|title=Clintons Tap Bing Pulse For Real-Time Audience Feedback At CGI Events.|url=http://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/228734/clintons-tap-bing-pulse-for-real-time-audience-fee.html|newspaper=Search Marketing Daily - Media Post|date=24 June 2014}}</ref>

=== Other ===
[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] included Bing Pulse in its online broadcast of the [[House Foreign Relations Committee]] hearing on the Bowe Bergdahl prisoner exchange in June, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/228734/clintons-tap-bing-pulse-for-real-time-audience-fee.html|title=Clintons Tap Bing Pulse for Real-Time Audience Feedback at CGI Events}}</ref>
[[CBS News]] used Bing Pulse in its "50 Years Later" program, a special about the [[Civil Rights Movement]] broadcast during July 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cbsnews.com/videos/civil-rights-50th-anniversary/ |title=CBS News: 50 Years Later, Civil Rights - Live Video Stream - CBS News |website=[[CBS News]] |access-date=2014-12-17 |archive-date=2014-12-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141217031536/http://www.cbsnews.com/videos/civil-rights-50th-anniversary/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
The Clinton Global Initiative leveraged Bing Pulse during their 2014 CGI University event at [[Arizona State University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pulse.bing.com/?post_type=casestudies&p=2431|title=Ambassadors of the airwaves}}</ref>
